title: Building resilience for cultural heritage in the face of climate change: Europa Nostra contributes to SD-WISHEES conference in Tbilisi, Georgia
content:
How can research, international cooperation and civil society advocacy help safeguard cultural heritage from climate change? And how can evidence translate into meaningful changes in policy, funding and practice? These questions were at the heart of the international conference Resilient Cultural Heritage: Building Bridges between Research, Policy and Practice, held in Tbilisi, Georgia, from 10 to 12 November 2026, within the framework of the EU-funded SD-WISHEES project.[1]

Photo: Courtesy of SD-WISHEES

The conference brought together researchers, policymakers, heritage professionals, civil society representatives and international organisations to explore ways of strengthening cultural heritage resilience in the face of hydroclimatic extreme events, including floods and droughts. Discussions addressed the links between water management, climate adaptation and the protection of tangible and intangible heritage.

Vanessa Fraga Prol, Advocacy and Partnerships Manager at Europa Nostra, represented both Europa Nostra and the European Heritage Hub, highlighting the role of civil society, international cooperation and heritage advocacy in climate adaptation and disaster-risk reduction.

title: Join the Online Masterclass ‘Balancing Heritage Conservation and Climate Action’ on 7 December 2026
content:
Europa Nostra and the Office of Public Works Ireland (OPW) are hosting the online Masterclass ‘Balancing Heritage Conservation and Climate Action on Monday 7 December 2026 (13:00-14:30 CET / 12:00-13:30 WET).

This masterclass explores the methodology, practical experience and key outcomes of the initiative Improving the Energy Performance of Heritage Properties in State Care, which has been developed by OPW to support the country’s climate action commitments and the EU’s decarbonisation targets. At the time, no clear framework existed for improving the energy performance of historic buildings while safeguarding their heritage value. The initiative offers valuable insights and lessons learned that can be adapted and applied in other contexts and settings. The initiative received both a European Heritage Award / Europa Nostra Award and the Grand Prix 2026 in the Education, Training and Skills categories.

Register now

This online masterclass is organised in the framework of the network project Europa Nostra Heritage Agora, which is supported by the Creative Europe programme of the European Union.
